scope: Automatic rotation and retention for configured file log sinks

defaults.daily_rollover: first nonempty write on a later UTC day

verification.editor: Real gopls completion, hover and definition include rotation fields and generated override keys

review: Zero file rotation limits resolve through one default policy; explicit disable preserves append-only behavior. File-only settings fail on streams/stacks.
Preparation does no filesystem I/O. Startup failure releases descriptors and the stable rotation lock. Shutdown serializes with writes and closes the active file before its lock.
Size and UTC-day rollovers preserve complete accepted records. Existing files append; oversized records reject before mutation. Replaced active paths reject rotation and recover after restoration.
Retention tests cover count, age, restart and ordinary-write cleanup. Only exact matching regular archive files are eligible; unrelated files, symlinks and directories survive.
Concurrent writers retain all records in the test budget. A second rotation owner fails; startup failures leave the file usable by a subsequent owner.
The independent configured application exercises TOML, environment settings, generated typed overrides, JSON record integrity, credential redaction and application shutdown.
No new dependencies or process-global services were introduced. Final source review required no corrections after the passing focused race tests.
limits: Cleanup runs at startup, rollover, or the first write after an hour since cleanup; idle applications do not run a timer.
File rotation uses macOS/Linux locks and requires one owner, a local operator-controlled directory, and no external file mutation. Network filesystems are unsupported.
Retention counts archives separately from the active file and may retain less than fourteen days under high volume.
Synchronous logging is not a durable audit ledger. Standard slog Logger methods do not return handler failures.
Linux binaries were compiled, not executed. This change does not claim new live-provider or performance certification.
